judged.rule: In every world and judged seed the independent checker names no violation of any rule: every flyer's home a declared perch; no flying position outside the volume or the kind's band; no landing, take-off or perch off a declared perch's column, and no perching flyer off its perch's point; no move longer than the kind's top speed allows in a step, the move into every episode and between windows included; no point of any move in a solid cell of the checker's own grid, other than its perch object's own while it moves along that perch's column; no move bringing a body, a box as wide as its kind's span, into a part of any object other than that; no perch holding two flyers; every episode's first step with every flyer perching at home.
At every episode's last step every flyer is perching at its home perch, in every world and judged seed, and every window names exactly the flyers the checker finds not home.

Every window the server's worker process serves (a spawned process computing whole episodes) has the digest of the window cut from the same episodes computed in the measuring process, in every world and judged seed.

On this lane's release server (a production build on slot 3 with a new synthetic workspace, the small square and seven more trees, 24 flyers), inside quiet-slot then gpu-slot behind the idle gate, in each of five runs, each after an edit so the flight read is cold, the slowest GET /healthz answer beside the cold flight read takes at most 25000 us.

record.question: With the flight's episodes computed by a worker process off the request path on the shared clock, searches for a route home bounded, and a checker that places every part and perch on its own, does the flight keep every flyer clear of every part and in its bounds, bring every flyer home at every episode's end, serve from the worker exactly the windows this process computes, and leave the server's other requests unslowed while a cold flight read is computed?

reported.what: The same five runs on main's release server at 465f2909, whose flight computes on the request's thread, the read asking for the window from the step before an episode ends. No target.
Each run's second read of the window it just read, as a page reading ahead finds it. No target.

Inside quiet-slot then gpu-slot behind the idle gate, in this checkout: the worker's spawn to its first answer, a cold episode of eight trees and of the cluttered square (24 flyers each) through a running worker, and one search for a route home that finds none on the largest grid the module admits, bounded and unbounded. No target.

Per run, the searches for a route home, those that found none, the most one flyer made in an episode and the most queue entries one search took (at least the cells it settled). No target: the bounds hold by construction, and this says whether they bound anything in these worlds.
Per world, the steps the guard refused. No target.
